summary: 52-year-old renal transplant recipient on tacrolimus, mycophenolate and prednisolone, 2 days of mild RIF/flank ache, T 37.4 °C, WBC 10.2, CRP 96; CT shows perforated retrocaecal appendicitis with a 2 cm collection.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Mild right-sided abdominal pain for 2 days
inputs.hpi: Renal transplant 6 years ago. 2 days of mild right lower abdominal and right flank ache, reduced appetite. Feels 'not right' but no rigors. No vomiting. Graft function stable at last clinic.

exam.abdomen: Mild tenderness in the right iliac fossa and right flank. No guarding. Transplant kidney in the left iliac fossa non-tender.

imaging.name: CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast
imaging.result: Perforated retrocaecal appendicitis with a 2 cm periappendiceal collection and localised extraluminal gas. No generalised free fluid.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Complicated appendicitis in an immunosuppressed patient
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Perforated retrocaecal appendicitis with a small collection in an immunosuppressed renal transplant recipient; signs blunted by immunosuppression.

socratesAnswers.site: Right lower abdomen and right flank

emergencyLevel.note: Immunosuppression blunts the signs; perforated appendicitis needs same-day surgical care.
emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: iOS: ClinicalPathwayEngine reads only CC/PMH keywords; CC 'Mild right-sided abdominal pain for 2 days' gives 'routine'. Web, since the engine-matching fixes (2026-09): this passed only because triage read negated phrases in the free text as positive findings (lost reasons: Systemic red flag symptom, Vomiting or possible dehydration). With negation-aware matching web triage gives acuity=routine, action=routine_booking, score=12: no triage rule covers this presentation.

redFlags.note: Immunosuppression should be surfaced as a risk factor (masked signs, higher complication rate).

mustInclude.note: Low threshold for CT when immunosuppression masks the clinical picture.
Patient on long-term prednisolone: peri-operative steroid cover. Quality: no single appendicitis-guideline statement.

guideline.name: WSES Jerusalem guidelines — diagnosis and treatment of acute appendicitis (2020 update)
guideline.section: Clinical scores (AIR/AAS over Alvarado), imaging by age/sex/pregnancy, antibiotic-first option, complicated appendicitis (abscess), antibiotic duration
guideline.citation: Di Saverio S, Podda M, De Simone B, et al. Diagnosis and treatment of acute appendicitis: 2020 update of the WSES Jerusalem guidelines. World J Emerg Surg. 2020;15:27.

rationale: Permutation: immunosuppression and diabetes. Signs and WBC are blunted; the engines must still keep appendicitis on the list, triage urgently, recommend CT and antibiotics and surface the immunosuppression.
